scope: Independent read-only review of the native MemoryPageTurn completion repair and one focused test execution. No source, ref, provider, workflow, timeout, or acceptance-gate edits.

conclusion.sourceLevelRiskReproduced: Without a delivered native animation callback, the former settle path could leave turn nonnull, accessibility hidden, and navigation controls disabled indefinitely. The owner retained three actual-component behavioral failures before the repair.
conclusion.runtimeAttribution: The b5 iPhone journey failed during initial Open book, before Next/Previous/swipe turns executed. This is an independently reproduced adjacent completion-contract risk, not a diagnosis of that run.

reviewFindings.finding: Native completion and the JS duration callback share the same done/dispose closure. The first terminal path clears the timer and retires pendingSettlement; repeated or late success/interruption callbacks do not commit twice.

The fallback retires its closure before calling progress.stopAnimation. Pinned RN TimingAnimation.stop synchronously notifies finished:false; the retired callback cannot cancel the chosen terminal result. Explicit cancellation similarly retires before stopping/resetting native work.

Identity/index sync, active=false, geometry/reduced-motion changes and live unmount cleanup use layout effects. Timer ownership is removed at those committed lifecycle boundaries, before a delayed passive cleanup could allow an invalidated completion.

JSON.stringify(pageIds) is collision-safe for the declared string-array input; JSON.parse supplies a matching immutable content snapshot to machine.sync. Equivalent arrays leave dependencies stable and preserve the pending turn. Distinct arrays such as [a|b,c] versus [a,b|c] invalidate it.

Both native timing and the fallback use the same memoryTurnDuration result. The shared file is unchanged: reduced motion is zero, otherwise max(120, round(560 * remaining progress)). No extra grace interval, deadline widening, or global timer/animation override was added.

A native finished:false delivered first cancels and unlocks. A duration completion chosen first ignores later native results. A committed turn remains locked in the existing state machine until the parent acknowledges the new index; no rapid duplicate page advance is allowed.

The existing single live media child and static adjacent previews remain intact. Cancelled settle restores pointer/accessibility state; successful settle unlocks after parent index acknowledgement. Reduced-motion taps still commit without a native timed turn.

Production diff is limited to the native component completion/lifecycle/identity implementation. Shared rules, preview design logic and web implementation match the published source. The parent reader remains responsible for book key, active route/modal conditions and committed index.

independentExecution.scope: Only tests/quality/memory-page-turn.cjs was executed; no broad suite, provider call, simulator or CI rerun.

ownerRunsInspected.stage: owner interim candidate before committed-lifecycle and collision fixes

coveredCases: withheld native completion for a tap
native success/interruption winning before the duration
cancelled and committed swipe settlement without a native callback
explicit cancellation and parent index acknowledgement
route inactivity, resize, reduced-motion change and unmount before passive cleanup
equivalent page-array refresh preserving the current turn
single live media child, authorized preview media and existing web/machine behavior

limits: The actual TSX component and shared rules execute through a controlled React-hook/native-host harness. The test does not run React Native, Hermes, UIKit/Android animation engines or a physical device.
Manual layout/passive scheduling demonstrates the reproduced committed-cleanup race; it is not a complete concurrent React scheduler.
The fallback cannot run while JavaScript is blocked, and therefore does not establish an absolute wall-clock upper bound or explain delayed b5 native event delivery.

At the intended duration, a runnable JS fallback may logically finish before a delayed native completion is delivered. That is the deliberate first-result contract, not proof the visual animation finished on time.
The existing callback ref publication and parent authentication/navigation lifecycle are not redesigned by this repair. No broader account/session acceptance is inferred.
Pinned installed RN source hashes identify the code read during review; this test is not a final app-binary attestation.
